content: The document outlines comprehensive guidelines for monitoring and managing HIV care and treatment, emphasizing a patient-centered approach. Below is a professional interpretation of the content: 1. HIV Care and Treatment Patient Card: This card is used to document critical information about a patient’s HIV treatment journey, including the initiation and progression of antiretroviral therapy (ART). It records the date ART began, any prior ART regimens, and whether the patient transferred from another facility. It also tracks the patient’s viral load (VL) and any changes in ART regimens, such as switching from first-line to second-line therapy. 2. Prior Antiretroviral Use: It also notes whether ARVs were used for HIV-exposed infants and the outcomes of such interventions. 3. Family and HIV Status: The card includes information about the patient’s family members, their relationship to the patient, and their HIV status. It also records the date of the patient’s first positive HIV test, confirmation of the diagnosis, and enrollment in HIV care. 4. Drug Allergies and Comorbidities: Any known drug allergies, chronic conditions, or concurrent medications are documented. This includes tuberculosis (TB) status, previous TB therapy, and any symptoms suggestive of TB, such as prolonged cough, fever, night sweats, or weight loss. 5. HIV-Exposed Infant Follow-Up: For infants exposed to HIV, the card tracks follow-up care, including cotrimoxazole prophylaxis, HIV testing, and final HIV status. It also records nutritional support and infant feeding practices, such as exclusive breastfeeding, replacement feeding, or mixed feeding. 6. ART Interruptions and Follow-Up: The card documents any interruptions in ART, including missed drug pick-ups, reasons for stopping treatment, and dates of restarting therapy. It also tracks follow-up status, including whether the patient was lost to follow-up, transferred to another facility, or deceased. 7. Baseline and Ongoing Monitoring: It also tracks adverse drug reactions, comorbidities, and coinfections, including opportunistic infections (OIs) and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). 8. Pregnancy and Reproductive Health: For women, the card records pregnancy status, reproductive health choices, and family planning methods. Codes are used to indicate whether the patient is pregnant, breastfeeding, or using contraception, and whether they desire future pregnancies. 9. TB Assessment and Management: At each visit, patients are assessed for TB symptoms. If TB is suspected, referrals or diagnostic tests (e.g., smear, culture, or Xpert MTB/RIF) are conducted, and results are recorded. If TB is confirmed, the type (e.g., pulmonary TB, extrapulmonary TB, multidrug-resistant TB) and treatment regimen are documented. Preventive therapy is initiated for patients without active TB. 10. Vaccination and Hepatitis Screening: For children, vaccination status is recorded, including vaccines such as BCG, hepatitis B, and measles. Hepatitis B and C screening is conducted for all patients, with vaccination provided for those who test negative for hepatitis B. For those who test positive, liver disease staging is performed, and treatment is determined. 11. Adherence Monitoring: Reasons for non-adherence to ART are documented, including forgetting doses, side effects, financial constraints, or stigma. Strategies to improve adherence, such as education and counseling, are emphasized. 12. Nutritional and Psychosocial Support: Nutritional counseling and support are provided, particularly for children with malnutrition or poor growth. 13. ART Regimen Changes: Reasons for substituting or switching ART regimens are categorized, such as toxicity, pregnancy, drug stockouts, or treatment failure (clinical, immunological, or virological). The card also tracks any treatment-limiting toxicities, such as gastrointestinal issues, skin reactions, or metabolic changes. 14. Patient Education and Prevention: Patients are educated on HIV basics, prevention strategies (including for key populations), and the importance of adherence to ART.
